column2: Unable to Correctly Render Colored Text in Ghost
column13:
imseanpan (2024-11-03T10:19:52Z): ### Update After further debugging, I found that the saved HTML used the `render` method from the `kg-lexical-html-renderer` package. Fortunately, I found the `render(): string` method in the `utils->TextContent.ts` file and discovered that the `node` object does have the `__style` property. However, the `LexicalNode` defined in TypeScript does not include this property. To verify this issue, I added the following experimental code: ```typescript // imseanpan add test code if (node.__style !== '') { const span = document.createElement('span'); span.setAttribute('style', node.__style); span.textContent = node.getTextContent(); currentNode.append(span); continue; } ``` It appears to be working successfully. Although my code ran successfully, it is not rigorous. Therefore, I'm just identifying the issue and confirming the problematic code location. If possible, I hope the official team can quickly fix this issue and add support for changing text color so that we can happily use Ghost. Thank you! | kevinansfield (2024-11-04T11:11:24Z): Style support for text was intentionally left out. I thought we also had a transform to strip style properties on the Lexical side of things too but I can't find that now. It's a design decision for our editor to provide minimal routes to creating poorly designed content and text color was a big part of that, not just for design but because of the accessibility issues that can create across light/dark mode and ensuring content displays correctly across different themes. On top of that, style attributes can leak across copy/paste into the editor which then creates a whole lot of other issues because there's no real way to undo that unless you add in support for editing all of the different styles that can be attached. As such I wouldn't consider this a bug. If you're looking to make changes in your own fork then the forum ([I see you've already duplicated your question there](https://forum.ghost.org/t/unable-to-correctly-render-colored-text-in-ghost/52144/1)) is a better place to get support.

\_If\_ we were to support text color it would likely be done via a custom property on our lexical nodes that is rendered as a class attribute. That way Ghost would be able to provide some default colours which can be overridden by themes, without hard-coded style attributes causing potential problems. | github-actions (2024-11-04T11:12:20Z): Hey @imseanpan 👋 We ask that you please do not use GitHub for help or support 😄. column2: Incorrect handling of German umlauts in permalink generation
column13:
sagzy (2024-09-16T16:08:25Z): Hey noezdev, thanks for raising the issue! 🙂

The letters `ä, ö, ü` are not translated automatically to the German-equivalent `ae, oe, ue` as this would be incorrect for other languages that also make use of the same letters (e.g. Swedish, Finnish, Estonian, Turkish).

Instead, we recommend choosing the right permalink for your post by updating the permalink in the Post Settings directly (cf. demo attached). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/269b4e18-3d52-450f-b11c-4e35192c4533
Hope this helps. 🙂 | noezdev (2024-09-19T09:30:45Z): Thank you for your response to my issue. I understand your point that converting special characters in the URL can be a challenge. Interestingly, this used to be the case with WordPress, but was later changed. There are a few possible solutions: * You could consider the set language of the page and adjust the conversion based on that. This way, the German rules would apply to German content. * Alternatively, you could create a conversion table that defines how certain special characters are converted into URLs. This would enable consistent handling across languages. Another point is that the conversion from “Ä” to “a” is also not optimal for all languages. In Swedish, for example, “ae” would be the preferred variant, not “a”. It would be great if Ghost could find a more flexible solution here that takes different languages and their particularities into account. Let me know if you have any further questions or ideas! @sagzy maybe you can re-open the issue?

```json
  "mail": {
    "transport": "SMTP",
    "from": "EMAILUSER",
    "options": {

      "port": 465,

      "tls": {

    }
  },

column2: tfuy
[fix] Improve sharp failure fallback
column13:
SaadBazaz (2024-05-14T06:55:27Z): I've found a temporary workaround, after going through some of Ghost's code. It seems like there is a check which prevents `sharp` from running at all, [here](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/842290cbef092ea438c5ea737342c3ecad90445f/ghost/core/core/frontend/web/middleware/handle-image-sizes.js#L109).

So the solution was to:
1. Enter the docker container
2. `cd ./current`
3. Run `yarn remove sharp`, and then,
4. Run `rm -rf node_modules/sharp`
To completely uninstall and clean `sharp`.

You would also need to add this to `config.production.json`:
```json
{
   ...
   imageOptimisation: false
}
```

Doing the above completely disabled sharp and now allows me to upload images (albeit, the images are a bit large, but I can make do :D)

I have been able to reproduce this in iOS Safari when the HTTP header `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` is present on the response for requests to `/ghost/auth-frame`. I'm thinking this is an issue with how iOS Safari is handling `204` responses with this header

This isn't a standard header that gets set by Ghost so I believe it is possibly coming from somewhere higher in the stack (i.e nginx adding additional response headers)

I'm not sure how much control you have over your environment, but you could try tweaking your server configuration to not include this header for this path to prevent this from happening for now whilst we explore other solutions 👍 | molly (2024-07-19T18:08:44Z): I've removed it for now, and it does seem to resolve the issue.

I'm using the default nginx configuration from the one-click Ghost install on DigitalOcean, so my guess is this is affecting others with the same. column2: Support Bluesky oEmbed auto-discovery
column13:
kevinansfield (2024-04-17T06:22:54Z): Bluesky oembed should already be supported via the `<link rel="alternate" type="application/json+oembed" href="...">` tag.

However looking at the oembed data returned it's missing a `height` property so it isn't seen as a valid oembed response. According to the [oembed spec](https://oembed.com/#section2) (See "2.3.4.4. The rich type") both `width` and `height` are required fields for the `rich` type. | bnewbold (2024-04-17T21:30:25Z): Hi @kevinansfield, thanks for the fast reply!

Our intention is to set `height` to `null`, which is what Twitter does (https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-for-websites/oembed-api#item1). We don't have a way to pre-compute height of an embed ahead of time, so we can't set an accurate height value. | kevinansfield (2024-04-17T21:40:55Z): Ok, taking a look at the code it seems we don't have validation steps for "known" providers handled by the `oembed-extractor` library which is why Twitter works. I think we should at least be able to [drop the `height` requirement here](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/main/ghost/oembed-service/lib/OEmbedService.js#L337) when checking that the `rel="alternate"` derived data is valid - we don't actually use the height anywhere, the check was just protection against potentially reading/storing/exposing data from non-oembed resources. | bnewbold (2024-04-17T22:11:05Z): Great, thank you!

We have `height: null` shipped out in prod now, FWIW:
https://embed.bsky.app/oembed?format=json&url=at%3A%2F%2Fdid%3Aplc%3Az72i7hdynmk6r22z27h6tvur%2Fapp.bsky.feed.post%2F3kq7ezofqak2f

column2: URLs of blogs changes to English even if I type the url in Hindi  or other languages
column13:
markstos (2024-01-12T18:09:04Z): This has been a recurring request and the latest web standards support non-latin characters in URLs. It is aligned with Ghost's goal to offer the platform in multiple languages now. Here's what I posted in the forum about this:

----
It used to be that such characters were not allowed in URLs, according to RFC 3986.

But according to the newer [WHATWG standard for URLS](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/), Unicode is allowed in URLs if the code points are in the range U+00A0 to U+10FFFD.

...

To me, this seems like be a bug in Ghost if Ghost is still creating URLs based on the older RFC 3986 standard for URL formats and not the WHATWG URL spec.

Ghost might be able to replace it’s current URL building library based on the old standard with one based on the new standard, like [whatwg-url - npm 2](https://www.npmjs.com/package/whatwg-url)

That's from:  https://forum.ghost.org/t/can-i-not-use-english-on-post-url/40348

See Also:

* https://forum.ghost.org/t/to-turn-off-automatic-url-translation-into-latin/1817

column2: Ghost fires updated webhooks before save/update is fully completed -  Edit lock, unable to save
column13:
kevinansfield (2023-10-14T11:39:11Z): This is expected, the web hook is firing at the right time but you're modifying a post whilst it's still open in the editor and therefore causing the editor and the server state to become out of sync in the same way as if someone else was editing the post. In this case someone else _is_ editing the post, it's just that it's a bot rather than a real person.

Whilst a post is a draft any changes are continually saved, each of those saves will trigger the post updated web hook.

Having an external tool modifying a post on every save will always cause this issue. I would suggest updating your external integration to only make changes when a post is published, although even then you'll run into the same issue if you continue to make changes in the editor after publishing. The web hooks system is designed to trigger changes in external systems, not to facilitate modifications of posts/pages whilst they are being edited. | mheland (2023-10-14T11:57:25Z): Hi Kevin, the strange thing is that the integration/hooks works on my VPS, does not generate a 
Edit Lock error, the integration updates Twitter/Facebook cards in the background on every save/update,
even when in Draft mode, and when editing published posts.

On GhostPro / digitalpress.blog hosting enabling the integration throws the Edit Lock error.

I'm talking to the people who made the integration (placid.app) - are there any new flags in the 
admin-API v3 to not request an edit lock or similar? 

Possibly related to GhostPro / digitalpress.blog using storage adapters and CDN's?



 | kevinansfield (2023-10-14T12:37:53Z): I can't explain how it's working on your VPS because if what you say the integration is doing is successful it will always break the ability to edit posts if it does it's thing whilst the post is open in the editor. Storage adapters, CDNs, or specific hosting setups won't have any effect as the out-of-sync detection is part of Ghost's core.

The flow looks like this:
1. The admin area saves and gets the updated post back with an `updated_at` value that matches what's on the server
2. The integration triggers and performs a new save causing the `updated_at` value to update on the server - there's no way for the admin area to know about this change
3. The admin area saves again but will send the `updated_at` value that it got in step 1
4. The server detects the mismatch and throws the error because it shows an unintentional overwrite of the last person to edit's work | mheland (2023-10-14T13:09:22Z): Thank you, seems I have an edge-case. Reminds me of previous job with Linux digital signage hardware where we had random reboots. A Linux kernel dev at $200/hr in a room with 50 mediaplayers, waiting for the the reboot to trigger on one of them. We called it the Neutrino Observatory. Pls close this and I'll continue talking to Placid to see if we can fix this. Tx /m

* [AMP is dead (for ranking)](https://forum.ghost.org/t/google-amp-is-dead/22827)

* [Google AMP in 2022](https://torquemag.io/2022/03/google-amp-2022/) . Conclusion: *this project is no longer as important as it once was.*

With the Ghost Content API, it seems that some third-party tools could call the API and generate AMP pages for those who want them, but AMP is far from being considered important to web performance and SEO like it once was.

As a small team, should Ghost continue to support it?

By querying the across all of the websites hosted on Ghost(Pro), they should check how popular is among their customers. 
 | daniellockyer (2023-11-08T15:46:21Z): To confirm - your message specifically relates to Google Ads/whatever Google Admanager is? Or do you have a reference to say that you need consent for all AMP pages?

It's not explicitly about ad sense only.

In Europe, a user must be made aware that a website is using third party services, no matter which these are. In most cases, a consent for the same is required. This does also apply to pictures from a third-party server, CDN services, etc.

Therefore, the configuration interface of Ghost should clarify that enabling a configuration (AMP for sure, but maybe even Unsplash) are reloading things from a third party website or even store cookies (which would require even a cookie consent). A statement explaining, that some countries may require the website owner to clarify this on a legal page/privacy page or imprint would be highly appreciated.

For reference:

You can find a couple of related articles and questions about this topic (also about google fonts or any other sideloaded content in general). Yes, it is a hassle to take care of the same. On the other hand, users not complying with the same are targeted by lawyers hunting for some quick wins.

- https://wordpress.org/support/topic/is-the-use-of-the-amp-plugin-gdpr-compliant/
-  https://ampforwp.com/ampforwp-is-now-gdpr-compliant-a-step-forward-towards-privacy/

samrap (2023-09-14T16:07:15Z): We're currently caching the endpoint (`/ghost/api/admin/newsletters/`, all query strings) for 15 minutes to alleviate some of the delays while this performance issue is worked out.  | markstos (2023-09-15T03:12:07Z): @samrap If you have MySQL 8.0.18 or newer, could you run this query and paste the result? It will help to understand how MySQL executing the query on such a table and using indexes.. or not. This is your query with "EXPLAIN ANALYZE " prefixed.

```
EXPLAIN ANALYZE select `newsletters`.*, (select count(`members_newsletters`.`id`) from `members_newsletters` inner join `members` on `members`.`id` = `members_newsletters`.`member_id` where members_newsletters.newsletter_id = newsletters.id and `members`.`email_disabled` = false) as `count__active_members` from `newsletters` order by sort_order ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC;
``` | samrap (2023-09-15T04:16:04Z): @markstos does this help?

```
-> Sort: newsletters.sort_order, newsletters.created_at, newsletters.id  (cost=0.95 rows=7) (actual time=0.095..0.124 rows=7 loops=1)
    -> Table scan on newsletters  (cost=0.95 rows=7) (actual time=0.047..0.064 rows=7 loops=1)
-> Select #2 (subquery in projection; dependent)
    -> Aggregate: count(members_newsletters.id)  (actual time=3144.770..3144.771 rows=1 loops=7)
        -> Nested loop inner join  (cost=24859.04 rows=4104) (actual time=502.030..3141.465 rows=42312 loops=7)
            -> Filter: (members.email_disabled = false)  (cost=10494.05 rows=9876) (actual time=0.019..75.984 rows=98226 loops=7)
                -> Table scan on members  (cost=10494.05 rows=98763) (actual time=0.018..64.572 rows=101275 loops=7)
            -> Filter: (members_newsletters.newsletter_id = newsletters.id)  (cost=1.04 rows=0) (actual time=0.030..0.031 rows=0 loops=687582)
                -> Index lookup on members_newsletters using members_newsletters_member_id_foreign (member_id=members.id)  (cost=1.04 rows=4) (actual time=0.029..0.030 rows=3 loops=687582)
``` | markstos (2023-09-15T10:05:27Z): Perfect @samrap. 

It shows what I suspected than an expensive full table scan is being used, in this case on members.email_disabled. 

If you are comfortable with doing so, you could try adding an index on that column and re-testing the SQL query, with and without EXPLAIN ANALYZE. If Ghost later adds an index there, you should remove the index before upgrading so it doesn't interfere with upgrade automation.  | samrap (2023-09-15T19:36:15Z): This is much better (~4.5s). Thanks for the help! @markstos  | markstos (2023-09-15T20:03:51Z): @samrap To confirm: Adding the index on `members(email_disabled)` solved the performance problem? 

That's great. I may see about making a PR to add that index for everyone.  | samrap (2023-09-15T20:12:28Z): It's a noticeable improvement. Here's my summary/thoughts:

- Adding an index reduced the execution time from ~22s to ~5s
- While this is a drastic improvement, it is still quite slow considering there are several XHR requests to the backend and this is just one of them
- All things considered, it's ~8s after initial render to have a fully functional post editor
- We'll continue to cache the HTTP response in addition to maintaining the index

Based on this I recommend adding that index as it is definitely an improvement 👍 

I wonder if you can look directly into the performance of your largest cloud users to get more insights? I'm genuinely curious since this issue only causes problems around 100k members. | markstos (2023-09-15T20:20:17Z): @samrap There might be more opportunities for indexes that are harder to see without the big scale that you have. 

MySQL has an option to start the server with a "slow query" log enabled (https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/slow-query-log.html),  and the Ghost logs already log some slow queries.

If you see more indication of slow DB queries that might benefit, let us know. 

When EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows a table scan for more than 10,000 rows, that's a strong indicator than index would help.  | samrap (2023-09-15T20:25:51Z): I'll keep you posted. We enabled slow query logs last week and so far it was only showing this one. But we'll be monitoring and I'll definitely update you if we see any others. 

I don't expect this to be a huge priority for you guys and really appreciate the attention/help.  | markstos (2023-09-15T20:44:23Z): @kevinansfield Is a DB migration the best way to add a new index ( [like this one](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/pull/12108/files)) the best way to add a new index or is there a better way? | shalabhtayal (2023-09-22T06:05:55Z): `SELECT n.id, COUNT(mn.id) AS count_active_members
FROM newsletters n
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT mn.newsletter_id, mn.member_id
    FROM members_newsletters mn
    JOIN members m ON mn.member_id = m.id
    WHERE m.email_disabled = false
) AS active_members ON n.id = active_members.newsletter_id
GROUP BY n.id
ORDER BY n.sort_order ASC, n.created_at ASC, n.id ASC;
`

In this query:

We use a subquery to select distinct pairs of newsletter_id and member_id from the members_newsletters table for members who have email_disabled set to false. This subquery filters the active members efficiently.

We then left join the newsletters table with this subquery on the newsletter_id to match newsletters with their active members. Using a LEFT JOIN ensures that newsletters without active members will still be included in the result.

We use the COUNT() function to count the number of active members for each newsletter.

Finally, we group the results by newsletter_id (renamed as id in the output) and order the result set as requested.

This query should perform more efficiently than the original one, especially when dealing with a large number of members, as it reduces the need for complex subqueries and calculations during the join operation. | markstos (2023-09-22T13:59:24Z): @samrap Could you run both the old and new queries and see how the results and and execution time compare for you?

benshaaw (2023-08-23T14:31:45Z): This being labeled as an error does feel misleading. In the past, an error would indicate the upload/activation of a theme has failed, whereas a warning could be raised by the upload/activation could still suceed.

Would it be possible to demote this error level, or better yet, only raise it if it is applicable to the current installation and/or theme? Our theme doesn't have a `page.hbs` partial, so doesn't seem relevant to us. | 9larsons (2023-08-23T16:19:09Z): The only errors displayed in Ghost admin (when not in dev mode) are errors. We've got two flavors of those, fatal and nonfatal. Fatal errors are what you mentioned - a warning where the theme cannot be activated - while nonfatal errors allow the user to still activate the theme.

We don't currently have a way to check for use of the `@page`-related features when activating a theme as theme activation only runs the theme through `gscan`. 

The intent here was to call out _potential_ loss of functionality, as indicated in the message. We can be more clear about that in the error message that is displayed and I've updated `gscan` to specifically call out the beta editor for this case.

As theme devs update their themes to use the `@page` feature(s) we both ensure that the themes are up to date with Ghost development and that Ghost+theme users get the best experience. This is definitely our recommendation.

Also worth noting is that while this only impacts the beta editor at this moment in time, the new editor will not always be in beta. | benshaaw (2023-08-23T16:32:53Z): > The only errors displayed in Ghost admin (when not in dev mode) are errors. 9larsons (2023-08-21T16:51:06Z): Hey @fueko, to clarify, the `@page` global should only be referenced within the `page.hbs` file or its partials. It should not be used within `post.hbs`.

As for the `gscan` error, users need to both update Ghost and their Reiro theme in order to not see the error. 

The theme error should only show in admin (the red box in the sidebar) when it's not the only warning. If it's the only warning, we don't show the box and users should only see the message in the Post editor sidebar.

Could you provide some more details on what users are seeing with their error?  | fueko (2023-08-21T17:07:53Z): Hi @9larsons! Thank you for your reply.

My themes do not use the page.hbs file because, according to the Ghost documentation, it is not mandatory and in this case the post.hbs file is used (and I am not in favor of duplicating files if it is not necessary):

![Zrzut ekranu 2023-08-21 o 18 53 53](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/assets/23366922/33478297-e931-4fb6-a539-9d455e885f18)

> Could you provide some more details on what users are seeing with their error?

There is no confirmation but I can suspect that it is an error displayed  as a pop-up when theme is activated. Also as I mentioned no error is no longer visible with me when I added it to the theme, GScan also does not return any error.

So I understand that this helper works with pages, but for the past few years the post.hbs file has acted as a replacement for the page.hbs file, which was not mandatory. So will this be fixed as it was before (by which I mean that it is correct to use this helper anywhere, be it in the final post.hbs or page.hbs application)? | 9larsons (2023-08-23T12:27:38Z): Ah, understood - thanks for reminding me of that! There's only a few cases users should be seeing:
- No unknown globals; this would be if they installed the new version of your theme in a narrow window of Ghost releases, as we very shortly thereafter released the `gscan` version that would pick up the `@page` helper
- Missing `@page` use; this would be if they have a recent version of Ghost and an old version of your theme, in which case they ought to install the newest version of your theme
- Unknown `@page` feature use; this would only be the case if you had used `@page.something` that we didn't expect (anything that's not `@page.show_title_and_feature_image`)

We can certainly improve the error message to mention that a Ghost upgrade is necessary, although that'll require a Ghost upgrade to be visible anyways. It would be helpful to know what specific error message they are seeing in case there's something else going on here.

column2: Ghost doesn't support IPv6-only hosts for sending email
column13:
daniellockyer (2023-08-11T06:48:26Z): Hey there, thank you so much for the detailed bug report.

A PR to fix this issue would be very welcome 🙂 | chairulakmal (2023-08-26T07:19:47Z): Hi @sybo-matthew 👋
GhostMailer uses [nodemailer@6.6.3](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/b545f234b2f77a385b6a09ef5bb6b6a2a44aba9e/yarn.lock#L7080) which accepts the workaround you mention: set the IP address as host and set the domain name as tls hostname.

Have you tried using the workaround in `config.production.json`?
If `Direct` transport doesn't work, perhaps `SMTP` would:

```
"mail": {
    "transport": "SMTP",
    "options": {
      "host": "::",
      "port": 587,
      "secure": false,
      "auth": {
          "user": "username",
          "pass": "password"
      },
      "tls": {
        "rejectUnauthorized": true,
        "servername": "smtp.server.cloud"
      }
    }
}
```

I was going to test this on my local instance until I realized my ISP doesn't support IPv6 yet 🥲 | sybo-matthew (2023-09-06T08:15:12Z): @chairulakmal So sorry for the late response but this worked like a charm. Thank you for the help. For anyone else who stumbles across this post in the future, let me leave you the tips you need to make this work. 

- set up the `config.production.json` as outlined above
- ensure that you have manually configured an IPv6 DNS server inside of /etc/docker/daemon.json. Mine is as follows:
```
"dns": [
	  "2001:4860:4860::8888",
	  "8.8.8.8",
	  "2001:4860:4860:0:0:0:0:8888"
  ]
```
Confirmed this works with all IPv6 compatible SMTP services I tested it with.  | imp1sh (2024-03-23T18:35:17Z): I vote for reopening this as there's only a workaround given. I consider this to be a bug as software should prefer using IPv6 over IPv4 instead of the other way around.

Most important to repeat @royalfig on the [forum](https://forum.ghost.org/t/theme-errors-after-update-to-5-56/40128/10).

**This error won’t cause your site or Casper to stop working.**

It's a warning that the theme is using a helper that doesn't do anything (yet).

We have a new feature that we're working on releasing. As part of that work, we've rolled out a missing check in gscan (it was there but not wired up 🙈) that identifies any `@global` helpers used in a theme that don't exist. Ideally, that check would have been there for years, to help anyone who installs a too-up-to-date theme on an old Ghost install, the same as we have for helpers like `{{match}}`.

Meanwhile, we've done the prep work to launch the feature by updating Casper, the default theme. But we've not shipped these changes, or the new helper just yet.

However, the automated release of Ghost on Friday picked up the changes in Casper unexpectedly - which is a bug as it's meant to work off of the latest release.

We've implemented a fix for the broken release process, and a fixed release will be shipped soon.

column2: Some image sizes created as 0 byte files
column13:
markstos (2023-07-19T20:43:05Z): I used to manage a site that had 36 million images. One of them was of an innocent looking dog named Mindy. Mindy ruined my weekend.

Every time someone uploaded a photo of Mindy, the server would enter a death spiral and eventually crash. But I did not know someone was trying to repeatedly post Mindy. I only new the web site keep death spiraling.

It took hours, over the weekend, to track down that this wasn't a normal coding problem, but ultimately a bug in the ImageMagick library triggered by invalid JPEG data in Mindy's photo file. ( The fix: use the GraphicsMagick fork ).

Maybe you've encountered a variation of the Mindy bug. You can test to see if specific photos reliably trigger it. If you find one, try running it through a photo processing app that rewrites the file-- any app would do. I'll recommend https://squoosh.app/  

This laundering might clean out any triggering corruption inside the original image.  If you can /still/ trigger the issue, I'll wager that either:

   1. Ghost has some kind of validation failure and should be rejecting the image earlier (too big?)
   2. Indeed, Ghost as an image processing bug, or more likely the upstream image processing library it uses.  | daniellockyer (2023-07-20T07:00:38Z): Ghost doesn't do any image processing itself, but we do use https://github.com/lovell/sharp. Would you be able to report the issue there w/ the sample file, and link to this issue please? 🙂  | jlopp (2023-07-24T11:13:54Z): Unfortunately I haven't been able to reproduce this issue, even if I publish another article with the same images. The only difference is that I'm not emailing out the post when I publish. | markstos (2023-07-25T15:40:32Z): Zero-byte files might also happen  if the disk filled up, and that could explain when it's not reproducible now. Even if you check the disk now and it's not full, it's possible the some logs got rotated, the system was rebooted or something else happened to recover disk space. 

If you have monitoring setup on the disk space, this could help to observe trends. For example, you might see that a disk is coming close to filling up each day, and the automatic log rotation happens and recovers enough disk space. | jlopp (2023-07-25T18:47:01Z): Don't think it's a disk space issue; this dedicated machine has 20 GB of free space and doesn't run any other software; looks like it only writes ~50MB of logs per day and logs get compressed once they're 2 weeks old, so a total of less than 1 GB of uncompressed logs. | markstos (2023-07-25T20:27:51Z): @jlopp Does it have two partitions like "/" and "/home" or a single partition? If Ghost happens to write to  `/tmp` was mounted in memory as a RAM disk, that could fill up if a temp file was larger than memory. (I haven't checked Ghost if it caches uploads in tmp).  | jlopp (2023-07-26T14:29:52Z): @markstos only a single partition for / | markstos (2023-08-02T15:19:16Z): I have seen zero byte files created by other tools when the fail during processing-- after the file has been opened but before it has been written. Still, without having a  possibly triggering file to test with, it's hard to know if the file is unusual or corrupted, if Ghost has a bug, or if there happened to be some resource contention during processing.  | markstos (2023-09-22T17:18:21Z): @jlopp You mentioned at the time you sent your post that it had several images in it-- presumably you could see them before they were published and they looked fine. This indicates that the image were successfully uploaded and, at least then, not-zero-byte. 

Because this issue is not reproducible and because it has some indications of a "disk full" scenario, I recommend the issue be closed as Ghost bug. 

Sometimes disks can run out of inodes even when they have disk space or there can be "phantom" disk space filling up a disk if log rotation isn't configured correctly. 

Having graphs of the disk space and CPU could help better diagnosis an issue like this in the future.   | jlopp (2023-09-22T18:17:56Z): Yes, and I've published several posts since then without seeing the issue re-appear. Will re-open if it happens again and I can surface any commonalities.

```

  "resize": false

To my Ghost config, it allows me to upload GIF's. But obviously not ideal as it disables optimizations of all other non-GIF images. | 1kevinson (2023-07-25T06:06:56Z): > Also experiencing this issue with GIF's. When added:

Does the difference "before/after" is huge for non-GIF images ? | markstos (2023-07-25T15:28:26Z): For some context, the default for `limitInputPixels` is 268402689 pixels. Some conversions:
 
  * That's 268 Megapixels
  * If the image was square it would have dimensions greater than 16,000 pixels per side.
  * A high resolution 4k screen has dimensions of 4096 x 2160

In other words, it appears this limit is set quite high for typical images. GIFs are not a typical image because it's more a video format-- it contains many frames and thus many pixels.

The GIF format is also horribly inefficient. The format is so bad,  that when large website display "GIFs", they are not actually using the GIF format, but they have instead converted the files to a video format where they be compressed much better. Like,  possibly more than 90% better.

I'm not not sure it makes sense to adapt Ghost to better support this ancient and bloated format that works like video but is actually an image format.

Consider converting the image to another format like `webp` or `mp4` before uploading it.

I think the guilty party is here: https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/main/ghost/core/core/server/data/importer/importers/data/PostsImporter.js

The problem is in the block of code starting at line 222.  There's a check for some very old import formats, but no mention of lexical at all.  Looks like someone missed adding lexical to this implementation when the beta editor went in?

Line 240: ```if (model.mobiledoc) { // a bunch of mobiledoc import stuff happens```
but then...
Line 275: ```} else if (model.html) { // converts the html to mobiledoc ```

Since lexical posts export with their html field populated, this results in posts getting imported that have both mobiledoc and lexical.

Updating your original issue with more details is great, but won't notify us, so please make sure you leave a comment so that we can see when you've updated us. | Gabriel416 (2023-06-02T01:02:37Z): > Would you be able to provide the CSV (or at least a redacted version)? 🙂 [test-member-import.csv](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/files/11630900/test-member-import.csv) | Rahulcheerio (2023-06-07T15:18:28Z): Can I work on this issue? | vershwal (2023-06-22T16:35:24Z): I was checking this issue and here are my findings. > On self hosted ghost, when trying to import a csv of member emails I get an error saying Cannot convert undefined or null to object. My csv is only one column with email as the header of it. The issue is not with number of columns but with the encoding of the file. The file you have provided is of type `charset=utf-8` I tried uploading two files with exactly same text, the only difference was that one file was `us-ascii` encoded and other was `utf-8` You can try uploading these files yourself:- ascii : [test-ascii.csv](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/files/11836971/test-ascii.csv) utf8 : [test-utf8.csv](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/files/11836946/test-utf8.csv) With the current code only ascii file will be uploaded successfully. This is because the current code does not handle the BOM characters that are generally present in the Unicode-based encoding files. Read here: [Byte order mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byte_order_mark) I figured out the issue when I saw this in my debug console 🤯 Here, _header === 'email' is false because there are BOM characters present. @Gabriel416 @daniellockyer Adding a PR to fix this. | Gabriel416 (2023-06-22T20:14:15Z): > Byte order mark Wow great find, really appreciate you working on this! | daniellockyer (2023-06-23T06:31:36Z): @vershwal That's a great find - thanks! Reading the guidelines or issue templates before opening issues can save you and project maintainers valuable time. | NathanC (2023-02-04T06:05:56Z): The documentation doesn't mention this, at least that I can find. Documentation can be buggy; I searched for a while outside of it too, found various discussions and issues that all seemed closed/resolved. There are two old issues that mention it, both are closed.

I'll ask in the forum, but @ErisDS it'd be nice if the docs were clear on this. If the feature isn't supported and there's not parity here, that's totally fine—it's already great you're offering this open source! Still, it'd be good to know when evaluating this for headless use.

My search use cases are really simple, so something like Algolia would be overkill. | markstos (2023-09-07T18:50:34Z): If you have less than about 10,000 posts, you could have a template that writes out the titles you want to search during build time. The search engine is then just essentially searching and filtering through that data structure of titles and possibly posts.

You could also use the Content API to grab all the titles and cache for a period on the client and again, the search function could essentially become a client-side filtering function.

I just tested keeping the Developer Tools open while using the on-site search and... it makes no network requests. That suggests, the post titles are already there on the client side, so Ghost itself appears to be working like that-- filtering through content that's already on the client. 

The beauty of this design is that's a perfect match for a "headless" blog, because no API calls back to the Ghost server are actually needed. It could be used even on a statically hosted blog.

Even if search can be implemented using the existing Content API, I agree it could helpful to provide some guidance there, since people might be looking for a "Search API".

I’m reposting my codebase investigation contained there in case someone finds it useful.

1. Navigation helper produces `navigation` template:
https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/9f3d8ec67dac95fd4e67834c483ba042e6ce836e/ghost/core/core/frontend/helpers/navigation.js#L89
2. Template is returned by Handlebars service:
https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/9f3d8ec67dac95fd4e67834c483ba042e6ce836e/ghost/core/core/frontend/services/handlebars.js#L17
3. Which uses theme engine to find (and then return) partial:
https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/9f3d8ec67dac95fd4e67834c483ba042e6ce836e/ghost/core/core/frontend/services/theme-engine/handlebars/template.js#L15
4. Partials are set in the engine when it is being configured with partials path passed:
https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/9f3d8ec67dac95fd4e67834c483ba042e6ce836e/ghost/core/core/frontend/services/theme-engine/engine.js#L12
5. Engine is configured when we active theme is being set:
https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/9f3d8ec67dac95fd4e67834c483ba042e6ce836e/ghost/core/core/frontend/services/theme-engine/active.js#L115
6. Active theme returns partials path when it knows about at least one partial:
https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/9f3d8ec67dac95fd4e67834c483ba042e6ce836e/ghost/core/core/frontend/services/theme-engine/active.js#L71
7. Active theme learns about partials from a [GScan](https://github.com/TryGhost/gscan) check:
https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/9f3d8ec67dac95fd4e67834c483ba042e6ce836e/ghost/core/core/frontend/services/theme-engine/active.js#L44

Executed a view query for all tables:
```
set foreign_key_checks=0;
...
alter table api_keys convert to character set utf8mb4 collate utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;
...
set foreign_key_checks=1;
```

column2: Overriding sodoSearch url and styles hyperlinks lead to broken search function
column13:
pbru87 (2022-12-10T18:43:53Z): **Update:** It was caused by a "_[CORS header 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' missing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS/Errors/CORSMissingAllowOrigin)_" issue, because I tried to load the resources from another domain of mine. I solved the issue by placing the resources inside my Ghost theme and changed the "**sodoSearch**" part of my **config.production.json** as follows:

```
"sodoSearch": {
  "url": "/assets/vendor/tryghost/sodo-search/sodo-search.min.js",
  "styles": "/assets/vendor/tryghost/sodo-search/main.css"
}
```
Now, it works like a charm. Therefore, I close the issue.

``` | ErisDS (2022-11-02T10:17:12Z): > The default SQL mode in MySQL 8.0 includes these modes: [ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_only_full_group_by), [STRICT_TRANS_TABLES](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_strict_trans_tables), [NO_ZERO_IN_DATE](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_zero_in_date), [NO_ZERO_DATE](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_zero_date), [ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_error_for_division_by_zero), and [NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_engine_substitution).
- From https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html

Ghost expects the default sql mode, and **requires** STRICT_TRANS_TABLES

I'll leave this open for the time being to:

1. Get this documented
2. Look at catching these errors and instead throwing something more specific like "Incorrect SQL Mode, STRICT_TRANS_TABLES is required.

If anyone would like to take on 2 that would be awesome. | nik-nazarov (2022-11-02T10:39:38Z): @ErisDS thank you for your reply, I've just update sql_mode to default value and now it works! | samrap (2022-11-02T19:34:33Z): @ErisDS @nik-nazarov  can you clarify what actually needs to be done here?

```shell

```
 | samrap (2022-11-04T02:31:24Z): @nik-nazarov Brilliant! Thank you | danquack (2022-11-04T13:41:42Z): There was a foreign key relationship on the products table:
```
SELECT TABLE_NAME,COLUMN_NAME,CONSTRAINT_NAME, REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME,REFERENCED_COLUMN_NAME FROM   INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE WHERE   REFERENCED_TABLE_SCHEMA = 'ghost'; 

...
| subscriptions                          | tier_id           | subscriptions_tier_id_foreign                               | products                               | id                     |
```

Where the product table had the key as NOT NULL:
```
show create table products;
CREATE TABLE `products` (
  `id` varchar(24) NOT NULL,
  ...
```

To fix this I disabled the foreign key check and then altered the table:
```
mysql> SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS = 0;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.07 sec)

mysql>  alter table `subscriptions` modify  `tier_id` varchar(24) not null;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.22 sec)
Records: 0  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0

mysql> SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS = 1;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.07 sec)
```

It appears this is the commit that caused the change https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/commit/3858f255b9f6a0fa8e65f73959adf1682c4b129e, not sure how the schema migrations are validated, but this at least can get folks up and running until a patch goes in.

If this is not fixable by the Ghost dev team, please close this issue and I will have to switch to another CMS. (I know that MariaDB is officially not supported. But fortunately, in the past the dev team fixed some things anyway) | b-turchyn (2022-11-01T19:48:29Z): This impacted me as well. The issue occurs in the subquery for counting conversions. MariaDB seems to struggle with referencing a table that is the more than the "parent" of the subquery. If the post WHERE clause is done more than one child down, the issue occurs. [This Gist](https://gist.github.com/b-turchyn/38bd50d881c0bd8f9d5c9c6c16dd8af4) has the original query and a manually updated one that produces the same results. Haven't run a query plan on it to see what (if any) performance impact would arise. A snippet of the original and updated queries: Original: ```sql SELECT `posts`.*, (WITH `k` AS ( SELECT `member_id` FROM `members_subscription_created_events` WHERE posts.id = members_subscription_created_events.attribution_id UNION SELECT `member_id` FROM `members_created_events` WHERE posts.id = members_created_events.attribution_id) SELECT count(*) FROM `k`) AS `count__conversions`, ``` Modified, working: ```sql SELECT `posts`.*, (WITH `k` AS ( SELECT `member_id`, `attribution_id` FROM `members_subscription_created_events` UNION SELECT `member_id`, `attribution_id` FROM `members_created_events`) SELECT count(*) FROM `k` WHERE `k`.attribution_id = `posts`.id) AS `count__conversions`, ``` (Unrelated: it seems like this query is retrieving `posts.*` multiple times. Probably not inefficient from a query performance perspective, but inefficient from a data transfer perspective.) Edit: the source of this seems to be at [core/core/server/models/post.js#L1363](https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/blob/main/ghost/core/core/server/models/post.js#L1363) (`conversions(modelOrCollection)`). | ErisDS (2022-11-01T22:14:59Z): Sorry for taking a couple of days to get to this. As of Ghost v5 the Ghost team are no longer maintaining support for any database in production other than MySQL 8. I've explained this a few times on the forum, but I'll also explain here: For MySQL5, MariaDB was a 100% compatible drop in replacement. Since then, the MariaDB team have opted to diverge and not keep compatibility with MySQL. Along side this, the ORM and query builder that we depended on to maintain compatibility have not matured enough or received enough contributions to fully handle the differences. These things combined left our tiny team with the burden of handling incompatibilities, and it was actively detracting from us being able to deliver new features. Therefore, as of v5 we declared MySQL8 the only DB supported in production knowing full well with the features we intended to build that at some point we'd hit a breaking change in MariaDB, which has now happened. Ghost is an open source project, and if there's an individual or preferably a group of individuals who want to take on the burden of supporting MariaDB, that is of course possible however I think that realistically the effort belongs in [knex](https://github.com/knex/knex). | zblesk (2022-11-07T20:48:16Z): Thanks to everyone here in elaborating. I've just encountered this error today, when I'd been trying to switch from MySQL to MariaDB and wondered if I'd just messed something up. Maybe I'll consider running an older version of Ghost instead. 🤔 I do not need any of the subscription features; and since I'm self-hosting low-traffic blogs on a small server I can't really enlarge, memory usage is becoming a problem. I run both MariaDB and MySQL. MySQL runs 3 Ghost blogs and nothing else, and has ~50% bigger memory use than MariaDB running 11 app DBs... | TheManchineel (2022-11-14T08:06:50Z): Any advice to migrate from MariaDB to MySQLv8? | ErisDS (2022-11-14T17:38:48Z): There's loads of discussions around this on the forum: https://forum.ghost.org/t/how-to-migrate-from-mariadb-10-to-mysql-8/29575 I'm going to close this issue now. If someone wants to take on the work of mariadb compatibility, we can reopen. | TemaSM (2022-11-15T06:31:30Z): Introduced by: https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/commit/22fe1c01de5bde5075ddb942bd8cba6e9e4d700f#diff-3149f93d170c65cd0c97a204a2d19c6102351b3c542c357aa342874699521237R1363 Seems to be that can be fixed by simple escaping of table's name (`posts.id` to \`posts\`.id) inside `whereRaw()`
